payload.author: gilbert-barajas
payload.body:
Thanks for the fast turnaround on this, @jonsaadfalcon — your root-cause matches exactly what I was seeing from the reporting side. The tell was that the filler text wasn't in any code path; it was the agent's own re-prompt output, which is why grepping for the string came up empty.

This is the path my actual use case hits: a local squad of agents driving tool-calls through the router with `stream: false`. So the unconditional `_handle_agent` route was silently swallowing every function call before it reached the model's `tool_calls` — `not request_body.tools` is the right gate, and keeping it as a documented opt-in (rather than removing the guard later) is the part I'd most want preserved.

Happy to be the manual-verification checkbox — I have the exact setup (agent registered + MLX backend) that produced #414. Point me at the branch and I'll run the original repro and report the round-trip back here.

payload.author: jonsaadfalcon
payload.body:
Hi @sanjayravit — your Windows-compatibility audit was the right shape, and #436 just landed on `main` with your full API surface (`get_python_executable`, `open_browser`) and most of your call-site sweep (oauth, livecodebench, install.sh, quickstart.sh, the two test files).

Two corrections from the adversarial review that I baked into #436:

1. `openjarvis.core.__init__` does NOT re-export `DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR` — that would have raised `ImportError` because the symbol lives in `openjarvis.core.config`, and re-exporting would force eager import of the heavy config module at every `import openjarvis.core`. `oauth.py` keeps `from openjarvis.core.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR` alongside `from openjarvis.core import open_browser`.
2. Test-side `get_python_executable()` is now wrapped in `shlex.quote()` before being interpolated into `shell=True` strings — Windows interpreter paths often contain spaces (`C:\Program Files\Python313\python.exe`).

You're already credited in the merge commit as `Co-Authored-By`. Closing this one as superseded — thank you for the careful work. The Windows cluster wouldn't have happened this quickly without your design.

payload.author: TX-Huang
payload.title: fix(ask): honor agent.default_agent from config when --agent is omitted

payload.author: jonsaadfalcon
payload.body:
Hi @TX-Huang — closing this PR because your fix landed on `main` as part of PR #362, a consolidation of five high-priority contributor PRs.

Your commit is preserved with your original authorship:
- **`c7f451fb`** — `fix(ask): honor agent.default_agent from config when --agent omitted`

A follow-up commit (`0217a901`) keeps the `tests/telemetry/test_energy_wiring.py` tests on the direct-engine path that they were originally designed for. Your behavior change correctly routes `jarvis ask` (no `--agent`) through `config.agent.default_agent` (default `"simple"`), but the autouse `_clean_registries` fixture wipes `AgentRegistry` between tests, so the eight CLI-driven energy_wiring tests would fail with `Unknown agent: simple`. The follow-up sets `cfg.agent.default_agent = ""` in their `_energy_config` helper — same pattern your PR already uses in `tests/cli/test_ask_router.py` for the two MagicMock-config tests.

This was a great fix — silently bypassing the agent layer (and therefore the entire persona system) for the most common command was exactly the kind of surprising behavior that erodes user trust. 🙏
